name: Sika UCS Pak
paste:
SIKA® UCS PAK: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sika® UCS Pak, December 2024, Version 01.05 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/h/sika_ucs_pak.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sika® UCS Pak where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (December 2024, Version 01.05).
1.2 Product description. Sika® UCS Pak is a powdered underwater/anti-washout admixture formulated to increase the cohesion of concrete to enable significant reductions in washout. Sika® UCS Pak is packaged in water soluble bags to enable ease of addition and handling.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. Sika® UCS Pak allows for the production and the improvement of concrete to be placed underwater. Sika® UCS Pak is mainly used for the following applications:
    - A wide range of applications where concrete is to be placed underwater
    - Marine construction
    - Piling concrete in porous ground

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sika® UCS Pak
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: Underwater/anti-washout admixture
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Certificates and test reports. Conforms to the requirements of BS 8443
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - BS 8443: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Certificates And Test Reports (p.1).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer. Sika® UCS Pak has the following characteristics and should be used in combination with a Sika® HRWR/Superplasticiser:
    - Strong increase in cohesion
    - Extended workability
    - Superior anti-washout properties
    - Provides improved integrity of concrete placed underwater
    - Less segregation and bleed
    - Reduced segregation and moisture loss to ground in concrete piles
    - Packaged in water soluble bags for easy dispensing
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: Powder blend of plasticisers and viscosity modifiers
    - Appearance and colour: Pale Buff Powder
2.6 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 0.400Kg water soluble bag (24 bags = sealed tub)
    - Shelf life: 12 months from date of production if stored properly in undamaged unopened, original sealed packaging.
    - Storage conditions: Store in dry conditions at temperatures between +5°C and +35°C. Protect from direct sunlight and frost.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 Substrate preparation. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (December 2024, Version 01.05) states no substrate preparation requirements.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (December 2024, Version 01.05) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Recommended dosage: 4-5 bags/m³ in severe environments (flowing water); 2-3 bags/m³ in moderate environments; 1-2 bags /m³ avoidance of static segregation in piles
4.3 Compatibility. Sika® UCS Pak may be combined with many other Sika products. Important: Always conduct trials before combining products in specific mixes and contact our Technical Service Department for information and advice about any specific combinations.
4.4 Dispensing.
    - Sika® UCS Pak should not be added to the gauging water.
    - Sika® UCS Pak should preferably be added at the batching plant with the aggregate or cement to support dispersion.
    - A wet mixing time, which is depending on the mixing conditions and mixer performance, of at least 120 seconds is recommended.
    - Underwater concrete needs to have high workability (self collapsing) in order to flow and compact. Underwater/anti-washout admixtures combined with superplasticisers require a long, slower mixing action to achieve a high workability.
    - When added directly to a truck mixer, the mixer shall rotate its drums at maximum revolutions for at least 1 minute per m³ concrete and a minimum of 5 minutes to achieve a uniform mix.
4.5 Application method / tools.
    - The standard rules of good concreting practice, concerning production and placing, are to be followed.
    - Cement contents should be at least 400 kg/m³ (total cementitious content) with a maximum water/cement ratio of 0.45. Typically the fine aggregate content should be >45%.
    - Laboratory trials shall be carried out before concreting on site, especially when using a new mix design or producing new concrete components.
    - Underwater concrete can be placed by skip, pump or tremie. However, care is needed not to allow the concrete to free-fall through a water filled pump line or tremie pipe as the turbulent flow produced will cause the mix to segregate. Pumping will normally produce the best results and minimise washout as only the top surface is usually exposed to the full effects of the water movement.
4.6 Notes on application / limitations.
    - When using Sika® UCS Pak a suitable mix design has to be taken into account and local material sources shall be trialled
    - Overdosing may cause an increase in air-entrainment
    - The compressive strength of underwater concrete may be slightly reduced by the inclusion of Sika® UCS Pak but this is often negated by the addition of a Sika® HWR/Superplasticiser.
    - The setting time of underwater concrete will be increased when Sika® UCS Pak is used. This extra time to set is often beneficial to the concreting operation as underwater concrete pours generally take longer to complete than conventional land based pours.
    - The air-content of the underwater concrete may be increased slightly due to the viscous nature of the mortar matrix preventing all entrapped air being released.
    - Support from our Technical Service Department is recommended.
    that will tend to lower the compressive strength. Cohesion and anti-washout properties will be increased which may lead to reduced workability of the concrete. There may also be an increase in set time.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, confirm the site conditions with the manufacturer. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Conditions to be verified. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (December 2024, Version 01.05) lists no application condition limits.
5.3 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.4 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sika® UCS Pak, December 2024, Version 01.05, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/h/sika_ucs_pak.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: Sika UCS Pak, version 22/07/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/w/MSDS%20Sika%C2%AE%20UCS%20Pak%20GHS7.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sika® UCS Pak, version 17/11/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/9/sds-sika-ucs-pak.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.1, and include the records in the project documentation.
